spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The strongest fact is an exact local cancellation: after decomposing (d,P²)=D1D2², the e3 divisor sum contains ∏_{p|D2}(1-α_{-2}(p²)), so S(d) vanishes whenever D2 contains a lower-range prime. Only square components supported above √X survive, and those are compressed into G and H factors.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Writing D=(d,P²)=D1D2² and each relevant e|D as e1e2e3² reorganizes S(d) by prime-exponent layers. The e2 sum becomes μ(D2)μ(e3), leaving ∏_{p|D2}(1-α_{-2}(p²)). Since α_{-2}(p²)=1 on P1 and 2 on P2, this product is zero unless D2|P2. For surviving D2, further gcd decomposition of N and e1 yields Euler products G and H and equation (51): S(D1D2²)=(1+o(1))G(P)μ(D1)H(D1)/(G(D1)G(D2)).

directed.representation_or_bridge: D1 and D2 encode exponent-one and exponent-two parts of the interaction with P²; P1 and P2 encode the two coefficient regimes. Their intersection makes the vanishing condition visible, while G and H compress the surviving local contributions into a form usable in the outer d-sum.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The cancellation depends specifically on the cube-free α_{-2} coefficients and their piecewise p² values. The many divisor and coprimality transformations, plus the extension to all S(X), are specialized and do not establish an analogous filter for other moments.
directed.uncertainty: This is highly formula-dependent, with dense divisor conditions that should be scan-verified. The zero-unless-D2|P2 conclusion and final factorization are stated unambiguously.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Near the 10^12-th zeta zero, the authors compare |P_X|, |Z_X|, and their product for X=26.31≈log γ_{10^12} and X=1000 over an x-interval covering twenty nearby zeros. P_X is computed from a finite von Mangoldt cosine sum, while Z_X is an unsmoothed product over one hundred nearby zeros using exp(Ci(|x+t0-γ_n|log X)). The text reports that individual X-dependence mostly cancels and the product accurately approximates ζ pointwise.
